title: Low-fidelity rendering mode and semantic tooltip API for accessible high-density time-series
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Dashboards with hundreds of series and dense sample rates are a common production workload for customers. Our current time-series components render at full fidelity (per-point DOM or high-resolution canvas) which causes jank, high CPU and memory on mid/low-end devices, and noisy screen reader output for SR users when many points are exposed simultaneously.

Proposal: Implement a guided "low-fidelity rendering" mode and a companion "semantic tooltip" API. Low-fidelity mode reduces visual and DOM detail for high-density viewports by using aggregated condensed glyphs, simplified axis markers, and GPU-friendly polygon strips. The semantic tooltip API surfaces a structured, screen-reader-friendly summary of the active viewport and hovered series (min/max/median/outlier count) rather than reading every datapoint. The API also exposes a small set of hooks for Eng to plug in batching/caching heuristics.

Goals:
- Reduce frame time and main-thread CPU by >40% on typical 2018 MacBook Air and mid-tier Android devices for 100+ series with 1k samples each.
- Provide an accessible and concise summary for SR users; avoid flooding the a11y tree with thousands of nodes.
- Preserve parity with current visual semantics (color, trend direction, hover focus) in a reduced-fidelity presentation.
- Keep surface backward-compatible: developers can opt-in per-chart or via theme tokens.

Design details:
- Rendering modes: full | low-fidelity | thumbnail. Low-fidelity switches to aggregated strip rendering with tone-based gradients to preserve trend. Thumbnail is for tiny widgets (<=48px).
- Legend behavior: in low-fidelity, legend toggles to a condensed view with inline sparklines and an overflow menu for hidden series. Hovering a legend item triggers the semantic tooltip summary (not per-point readout).
- Semantic tooltip schema: {"seriesName","visibleRangeSummary","statBuckets","focusTime","recommendation"} (will be delivered as a flattened string for SRs; internal contract documented).
- Keyboard navigation: provide a single ORB focusable element for the chart that opens a summarizing panel for SR and keyboard users; arrow keys cycle series summaries rather than iterating DOM points.
- Visual fallbacks: for devices lacking WebGL, fall back to simplified canvas with lower draw calls and pre-baked bitmap tiles.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Prototype implemented in the component library with a toggle, documented token controls, and sample pages.
2) Performance tests show >=40% reduction in main-thread work on defined device profiles (benchmarks stored in confluence attachment).
3) Screen reader testing shows concise summary readout and keyboard-only workflow validated with two internal a11y testers.
4) API docs and migration guide published; feature flagged for gradual rollout.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Low-fidelity visuals might obscure precise outlier values; mitigated by exposing a drill-down mode and tappable summary to reveal full-fidelity view on demand.
- Additional surface area for SDKs and Eng integration (semantic schema stability). We'll version the tooltip schema and provide adapters.

Implementation notes for Eng:
- Prefer shader-based strip rendering (GPU) when available and fallback to batched canvas draw calls.
- Provide hooks to reuse the existing KV-cached aggregates from the serving-side telemetry (PM/Backend team collaborating).
- Add feature flag and a runtime metric (count of charts in low-fidelity mode) to measure adoption and unexpected regressions.

Design artifacts and links:
- Low-fidelity redlines and token table: https://drive.redwood.ai/designs/low-fidelity-rendering-v1.pdf
- Accessibility test checklist and transcripts: https://drive.redwood.ai/a11y/chronicle-summary-tests.xlsx

Next steps:
- [Design] Finalize token set for low-fidelity (color steps, stroke widths, glyph density) — Sofia (due 2026-02-19).
- [Eng] Spike GPU strip rendering and canvas fallback (ENG-40321) — Marco (in parallel).
- [PM] Schedule canary release for a subset of customers (PM-912).

Notes about uniqueness: This ticket focuses on a "semantic-first" approach: making the chart communicate meaningfully to assistive tech instead of reproducing raw sample lists, combined with performance-first rendering choices targeted at dense workloads.
